title: Thus I Resolv'd Before the Lord
description: Thus I Resolv'd Before the Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 39, part 1, headed “Watchfulness over the tongue; or, Prudence and zeal”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thus I re-solv'd be-fore the Lord, "Now will I watch my tongue, "Lest I let slip one sin-ful word, "Or do my neigh-bour wrong."

lines: Thus I resolv'd before the Lord,
"Lest I let slip one sinful word,
And if I'm e'er constrain'd to stay
I'll set a double guard that day,
Nor let my talk be vain.
I'll scarce allow my lips to speak
Lest scoffers should th' occasion take
Yet if some proper hour appear,
But let the scoffing sinners hear
That I can speak for God.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
